summary: Over 14 days this AAPS closed-loop system showed good CGM data quality (98.7% coverage) but zero logged carbohydrate entries, which blocks direct validation of carb ratios and meal-bolus timing. Overall time-in-range was 86.0% with elevated variability (CV 32.6%), including several level-2 hypoglycemia clusters (Aug-13, Aug-14, Aug-21) and severe hyperglycemia clusters (Aug-15, Aug-18). A profile switch to the current flat-ISF, u200 dilute-basal configuration occurred mid-period (Aug-13), adding uncertainty about its applicability to the first six days. Two recurring daytime windows (approximately 07:00-10:00 and 11:00-17:00 local, peaking near 16:00 local) show the most pronounced rises and correction-bolus activity, but at least two plausible explanations remain unresolved for each pattern (basal sizing, unannounced meals, dynamic-ISF behavior, and temporary-target interactions with SMB). Automation was found to already be operating at its safety ceiling during the two worst hyperglycemia episodes, which argues against automation under-responsiveness as the primary cause. No profile or core AAPS parameter change is independently supported by current evidence; the most useful near-term step is targeted meal/carb-timing observation before any dosing parameter is adjusted.

analysis_steps.findings: CGM coverage 98.7% (3995/4046 expected), ~5 min cadence, 0 duplicates, 0 invalid entries, 10 gaps (largest 65 min). Zero carbohydrate entries exist anywhere in the 14-day window. A Profile Switch to the currently authoritative flat-ISF, u200 dilute-basal profile occurred mid-period (2026-08-13T21:23Z), so applicability of the current profile to 2026-08-07 through 2026-08-13 relies on the user's declared historical_applicability rather than direct telemetry linkage.

analysis_steps.findings: Aggregate glucose: average 121.6 mg/dL, SD 39.7, TIR 86.0%, TAR 8.9%, TBR 5.1%, CV 32.6%. Level-2 hypoglycemia clusters on Aug-13 (down to 42 mg/dL), Aug-14 (down to 41 mg/dL), and Aug-21 (42 mg/dL). Severe hyperglycemia clusters on Aug-15 (up to 293 mg/dL) and Aug-18 (up to 290 mg/dL). An Occlusion and Pump Error announcement on Aug-19 coincides with elevated TAR that day, representing a plausible device-related confound independent of settings. A bolus-stacking pattern preceded the Aug-14 hypoglycemia cluster.

analysis_steps.findings: Overnight 03:00-07:00 local shows strong control (TIR 95.2-98.7%). The 00:00-01:00 local window shows elevated time-below-range (11.4% and 18.5%) with at least two competing explanations (the 00:00 basal segment of 0.6 U/h, the 90 mg/dL overnight target combined with aggressive UAM, or a residual effect of an unlogged evening correction) that current data cannot separate. The 16:00 local hour shows the day's worst pattern (average 162.8 mg/dL, TAR 32.1%) and coincides with the lowest basal segment (0.5 U/h), but automation independently reached its maximum-basal safety ceiling during comparable severe excursions on other days, which favors an unannounced-meal or UAM-detection-lag explanation over a simple basal deficit.

analysis_steps.findings: Carb ratio validation is fully blocked because zero carbohydrate entries exist in the data. The profile ISF is a single flat segment (56 mg/dL/U); the Dynamic ISF automation layer (70% adjustment factor) produces effective per-cycle sensitivity from 27.8 to 178.7 mg/dL/U around this baseline, which is expected behavior for that feature rather than demonstrated evidence that the flat baseline itself is wrong. No quiet, low-deviation baseline period exists to isolate the true flat-ISF need from Dynamic ISF's real-time modulation. DIA (10 hours) is long relative to typical rapid-acting settings but plausible given the declared u200 dilute-insulin context; no telemetry contradicts it.

analysis_steps.findings: Autosens disabled together with Dynamic ISF enabled is an internally consistent, non-conflicting configuration. Observed sensitivity_ratio values near 1.0 represent a neutral adjustment layer, distinct from the wider variable_sens dynamic-ISF swings noted in profile_cr_isf_dia. The effective max-basal ceiling (approximately 4 U/h, consistent with max_daily_safety_multiplier of 5.0 applied to the highest basal segment) was reached during the two most severe hyperglycemia episodes (Aug-14 and Aug-21), with insulin requested exceeding what could be delivered, indicating automation was already maximally engaged rather than under-responsive. Max IOB (25 U) was never approached (highest observed 5.935 U).

All sampled treatment and therapy-response entries are typed only as Correction Bolus or Temp Basal, confirming meal coverage is delegated entirely to SMB/UAM. Morning (07:00-10:00 local) and midday/afternoon (11:00-17:00 local) windows show recurring rises with correction responses that do not fully arrest the rise within 6 hours, while the evening window (18:00-21:00 local) shows smaller, more effective corrections.

Every identified hyperglycemia and hypoglycemia pattern in this dataset has at least two unresolved, plausible competing explanations, primarily because zero carbohydrate data exists to separate meal effects from basal, ISF, target, or automation effects. Automation was already operating at its safety ceiling during the worst excursions, which argues against increasing automation aggressiveness as a first step. The single most supported and lowest-risk next action is targeted meal and carb-timing observation in the two flagged daytime windows, which would unblock carb-ratio validation and basal/ISF attribution in the next review cycle. No profile or core AAPS parameter change is independently supported by current evidence; the temporary-target/SMB interaction and the overnight-low cause remain open clarification items for the user and care team.

strengths.finding: CGM data quality is strong: 98.7% coverage, consistent ~5 minute cadence, zero duplicate or invalid entries across 14 days, which supports confident time-based analysis.

Overnight fasting-like window (03:00-07:00 local) shows excellent control, with time-in-range between 95.2% and 98.7% and low variability, suggesting the early-morning basal and target combination is currently well matched to that period.
The evening window (18:00-21:00 local) shows comparatively stable glucose with small, effective correction boluses, indicating this part of the day is functioning well under the current settings.

Maximum insulin-on-board safety limit (25 U) was never approached (highest observed 5.935 U), and the max-basal safety ceiling engaged as designed during severe excursions rather than being exceeded, indicating the core safety limits are functioning as intended.

issues.finding: Zero carbohydrate entries exist across the entire 14-day period, which blocks direct validation of carb ratios and prevents separating meal-driven glucose rises from basal, ISF, or automation effects.
Level-2 hypoglycemia clusters occurred on Aug-13, Aug-14, and Aug-21 (down to 41-42 mg/dL), with the Aug-14 event preceded by two correction boluses given roughly 10 minutes apart.
Severe hyperglycemia clusters occurred on Aug-15 and Aug-18 (up to 293 and 290 mg/dL respectively), and coefficient of variation (32.6%) is elevated for the period overall.

A profile switch to the currently authoritative configuration occurred mid-period (2026-08-13), creating uncertainty about whether the first six days of data reflect the same settings being evaluated.

Recurring 135 mg/dL Temporary Targets overlap in time with elevated time-above-range on Aug-17 and Aug-18, and combined with smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled=false could suppress SMB delivery during those windows; the intended purpose of these temporary targets is not documented in the data.

An Occlusion and Pump Error announcement on Aug-19 coincides with elevated time-above-range that day, representing a device-related confound that should not be attributed to profile or automation settings.

education.note: Time-in-range, time-above-range, and time-below-range describe the percentage of readings within, above, and below a target glucose band, and are commonly used alongside average glucose and coefficient of variation to describe overall control and variability.

A sensitivity_ratio near 1.0 in loop status data represents a neutral, near-baseline adjustment; it is a different signal from the wider variable sensitivity values produced by Dynamic ISF, which recalculates an effective ISF each cycle based on recent glucose deviation.

When SMB/UAM automation is not paired with carbohydrate entry, carbs-on-board will always read zero, and SMB activation conditions tied to carbs-on-board (such as smb_with_cob_enabled) will remain structurally inactive; this is expected, not necessarily a malfunction.
A duration field in a loop status entry typically reflects the length of a temporary basal rate, not the configured SMB delivery interval; these are separate settings and should not be conflated.

Extended carbohydrates (e-carbs) and a pump's extended or dual-wave bolus are different mechanisms; e-carbs are entered as a carbohydrate absorption model over time, while an extended bolus is an insulin delivery method, and neither can be inferred from the other without direct logging.

safety_notes: This is decision-support content only; it does not provide medical advice and does not modify AAPS or pump settings automatically.
Independently verify every proposed change or observation plan with a qualified care team before acting on it.
If any profile or AAPS setting is changed in the future, change only one setting at a time and monitor glucose closely afterward.
Do not change basal segment sizing and the max_daily_safety_multiplier-driven basal ceiling at the same time, since one affects the other.

The hypoglycemia clusters identified on Aug-13, Aug-14, and Aug-21, and the severe hyperglycemia clusters on Aug-15 and Aug-18, warrant direct discussion with a care team regardless of any settings review.
The Aug-19 occlusion and pump error event should be reviewed with the device manufacturer or care team as a potential delivery issue separate from profile or automation settings.
